correctness.rationale: For every unweighted simple cycle of order at least three, the proof reconstructs all traces: singletons and pairs are shattered, a triple has an all-positive path and a missing-middle-pair trace only if its extreme vertices are antipodal, and both semicircles explicitly realize all eight traces. Four vertices on a shortest path contain two vertices at subdiametral distance with an intervening point, preventing a required trace. Counting unique antipodal pairs yields all coefficients. In even order, every triangle is a face of a unique matched-pair tetrahedral boundary; deleting one face per tetrahedron produces a disk union homotopy equivalent to the complete graph on matched pairs, and null-attached faces add exactly one two-sphere each. A deterministic finite checker tests every one-through-four support and mod-two boundary ranks for n=3..18; finite tests are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact all-order shattering complex resolves the mathematically natural ambiguity that occurs when shortest paths have ties. It explains a sharp odd/even VC jump and derives an explicit mixed-dimensional integral homotopy type, not merely a scalar dimension bound. Its coefficientwise and topological invariants characterize a useful canonical range space and separate geodesic paths from unique path systems, graph balls, and geodesic convexity. The precise count and sphere multiplicities are naturally forced by antipodal pairs, not selected arbitrary finite parameters.
